SQL:
WITH _base AS (
  SELECT
    customers__regions.name AS "orders.customers.regions.name",
    customers.city AS "orders.customers.city",
    CAST(SUM(orders.amount) AS DOUBLE) AS "orders.city_revenue"
  FROM orders AS orders
  LEFT JOIN customers AS customers
    ON orders.customer_id = customers.id
  LEFT JOIN regions AS customers__regions
    ON customers.region_id = customers__regions.id
  GROUP BY
    customers__regions.name,
    customers.city
), _cm_orders__amount_sum_partition_by_customers_regions_name AS (
  SELECT
    customers__regions.name AS "orders.customers.regions.name",
    CAST(SUM(orders.amount) AS DOUBLE) AS "orders.region_revenue"
  FROM orders AS orders
  LEFT JOIN customers AS customers
    ON orders.customer_id = customers.id
  LEFT JOIN regions AS customers__regions
    ON customers.region_id = customers__regions.id
  GROUP BY
    customers__regions.name
)
SELECT
  _base."orders.customers.regions.name",
  _base."orders.customers.city",
  _base."orders.city_revenue",
  _cm_orders__amount_sum_partition_by_customers_regions_name."orders.region_revenue"
FROM _base
LEFT JOIN _cm_orders__amount_sum_partition_by_customers_regions_name
  ON _base."orders.customers.regions.name" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM _cm_orders__amount_sum_partition_by_customers_regions_name."orders.customers.regions.name"
ORDER BY
  _base."orders.customers.regions.name" ASC,
  _base."orders.customers.city" ASC
LIMIT 21

args.message: The table has one row per region and city. Each row shows the city's revenue (sum of order amounts) and the total revenue of its region. Region and city both come from the customer who placed the order, and the region name comes from the customer's region ID. Oslo appears under both North and South because customers in different regions list Oslo as their city. Orders with no known region form one group with a region total of 1,193.30. That group splits into Paris (677.83) and a group where the city is also unknown (515.47).
